```{r setup}

# Packages
if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(tidyverse,
               palmerpenguins,
               gapminder,
               gt,
               scales,
               ggthemes)

# Brand palette/fonts — mirrors the variables defined in dataviz-best-practices.scss.
# (It's a hassle for R to read SCSS, so just repeating the hex values here.)
brand <- list(
  bg        = "#F9EBDC",
  primary   = "#317168",
  secondary = "#9D792F",
  accent    = "#F1655F",
  dark      = "#292F20",
  muted     = "#94a3b8",
  gratuitous = "#725496"  # deliberately off-brand, for the "before" examples
)

font_serif <- "Plantagenet Cherokee"
font_sans_serif <- "Halyard Text"

```

```{r data}

# Time-series data: monthly data from the economics dataset
df_unemployment <- economics |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2009-01-01"), date <= as.Date("2009-12-01"))

df_psavert <- economics |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2009-01-01"), date <= as.Date("2009-12-01"))

# Summary table data: gapminder, 2007 snapshot by continent
df_continents <- gapminder |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarise(
    countries    = n(),
    mean_lifeExp = mean(lifeExp),
    total_pop    = sum(as.numeric(pop))
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_pop))

```

# Why are so many slide decks [so bad]{.emphasis}? {background-color="var(--divider-bg)"}


## normative conformity

> "the tendency of individuals to adjust their behavior, attitudes, or beliefs to align with the perceived standards or expectations of a group or society"


## normative conformity…for slide decks

> "the tendency of employees to adjust their presentations to align with the perceived standards of their organization"


## normative conformity…illustrated {.statement}

"This slide deck is killing me."

. . .

"Let me produce another one."
